items.title: AFCS: Flown as a Sortie
items.description: Every layer of the flight control system taken where you meet it — ramp to approach — including the two numbers that explain all three hardovers.

items.title: Electrical: Counting Down the Layers
items.description: Two generators, two converters, a backup and a battery — and what each layer costs you as it goes, down to why the gear must come down early.

items.title: Hydraulics: What the Aircraft Isolates
items.description: Five systems, two valves that close on a leak before you touch anything, and the drills that follow from what the aircraft already decided.

items.title: Fire: Where the Agent Actually Goes
items.description: Five infrared detectors, three arm buttons, two bottles — and the fact that the number two engine and APU share a compartment for extinguishing.

items.title: Main Gearbox: Five Seconds, Ten Minutes
items.description: The tightest clock in the manual — bypass within five seconds, failure possible in under ten — and the five symptoms that override everything.

items.title: RIPS: Reading the Rhythm
items.description: How rotor deicing actually works, what a healthy cycle feels like in torque and vibration, and how to tell when you are outside the envelope.

items.title: EGPWS: Which Protections Are Actually On
items.description: Basic modes against look ahead, every threshold and aural, and the inhibits that switch protection off without announcing it.

items.title: Traffic & Weather: What Is Out There
items.description: Traffic advisories only on this aircraft — no resolution advisories — plus what the radar cannot see, and why a blue field is the dangerous one.
